cases.purpose: Verify %PPID removes the actual builtin caller after a positive control.
cases.comparison: Exact contract output and status; diagnostics checked for presence only
cases.script:
IFS= read -r name < /proc/$BASHPID/comm || exit 10
self=$BASHPID
pidof "$name" >control || exit 11
read -r -a ids <control
seen=no
for id in "${ids[@]}"; do [[ $id == "$self" ]] && seen=yes; done
[[ $seen == yes ]] || exit 12
pidof -o %PPID "$name" >omitted
rc=$?
[[ $rc == 0 || $rc == 1 ]] || exit 13
read -r -a ids <omitted || :
for id in "${ids[@]}"; do [[ $id != "$self" ]] || exit 14; done
printf 'invoking shell omitted\n'

cases.purpose: Illegal omit values are skipped with a warning and the lookup still runs. A missing name then exits 1 with empty stdout. +1 is a legal omit of pid 1.
cases.oracle: sysvinit-utils 3.14 pidof skips an illegal omit value and keeps looking
cases.comparison: Exact contract output and status. Illegal omits exit 1 with empty stdout; a nonempty stderr must name an illegal omit pid. +1 is legal and stays silent.
cases.script:
for value in 0 not-a-pid '' , 1,,2 1: 1:-2 -1 +1 4294967296 999999999999999999999999; do
  pidof -o "$value" no_such_pidof_7c3e >out 2>err
  rc=$?
  if [[ $rc != 1 || -s out ]]; then
    printf 'invalid omit handled incorrectly: <%s> status=%s\n' "$value" "$rc"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [[ $value == +1 ]]; then
    [[ ! -s err ]] || { printf 'legal omit warned: <%s>\n' "$value"; exit 1; }
  elif [[ -s err ]] && ! grep -q 'illegal omit pid value' err; then
    printf 'unexpected omit diagnostic: <%s>\n' "$value"
    exit 1
  fi
done
printf 'invalid lists rejected\n'
